text:
sanjay: Heads-up — after turning on the BF4/CUTLASS mixed-precision path in the sm90 pool we're seeing a +10-12% p95 regression for long-chat workloads. KV cache heat looks noisy. attaching quick profiler snippet and notes.

maya: Can you paste the perf snippet and which binary (triton runtime vs native cutlass) you rolled?

sanjay: We flipped the toggle via RW_ENABLE_BF4=1 + RW_CUTLASS_TOGGLE=experimental on canary. Runtime is Triton with CUTLASS kernels. Quick output: 

```
profile: endpoint=chat.long, seq=2048
per_token: 9.6ms -> 10.7ms (+11.5%)
kernel: cutlass_bf4_gemm (hot) 48ms -> 53ms
kvcache: miss_rate 0.18 -> 0.33
batching: avg_wait 1.8ms -> 2.9ms
arch_probe: detected sm86 but GPU reports sm90 in nvidia-smi (driver probe mismatch)
```

sanjay: note the arch_probe mismatch — looks like fallback to generic kernel when triton decides sm86 path, so cutlass kernel compiled for sm90 isn't used.

kevin: ah that explains *some* of the regression. If Triton picks the generic fallback the kernel will be slower and not leverage bf4 paths. Which build flags did you use?

maya: also: KV miss rate spike + batching wait increase = compounded latency. If prefetch/warmup isn't priming the kvcache, batching will hold requests longer waiting for prefetch hits. :thinking:

elaine: FYI I saw a similar symptom last month when the prober returned wrong arch after a driver update. We set -DUSE_SM90=ON in cutlass, but the runtime probe returned sm86 so it fell back at runtime. Actionable: re-run arch-prober on those nodes and check /sys/module/nvidia/version vs nvidia-smi.

ryan: infra-bot kicked canary rollback at 1965432130 due to latency alert. How large was the canary?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollback executed for bf4-experimental on sm90 pool at 1965432130. Rollback scope: 5% of capacity -> 0%. Alert: latency_p95 > threshold. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Next steps I propose: (1) re-run arch-prober + capture probe logs (probe_binary --dump), (2) add a safety check in the kernel selector to compare probe vs nvidia-smi and avoid mismatches, (3) disable bf4 toggle for pools where probe mismatch exists, (4) instrument KV miss vs batch wait telemetry (one datapoint per route).

maya: I can add a quick perf test job that toggles RW_KVCACHE_PREFETCH=0/1 and measures p95 to isolate prefetch effect. Also will run small microbench to confirm whether fallback path is slower ~+15%.

elaine: I'll raise an infra ticket to coordinate driver/prober parity and nominate nodes for a full rebuild if needed.

sanjay: thanks. For now rolling back and adding a canary gating step that compares arch_probe output to expected build matrix before enabling bf4. Also we should log an event when kernel fallback happens: e.g., "kernel_selector.fallback_reason=probe_mismatch" — helps triage in future.

maya: ack — I'll create the perf job and add a small alert for kvcache_miss_rate > 0.25 correlated with batch_wait > 2ms.

ryan: note: add a quick kill-switch env var so we can disable experimental cutlass path at runtime without deploy.

kevin: I can PR the kernel-selector guard and the telemetry keys. will ping owners for review.

sanjay: perfect. thanks everyone.

maya: thanks — will post perf job results in this thread when ready. :mag:
